Problem Properties

By: Annalise Lubbe | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When a deathtrap excavation site claimed the lives of two young people, questions were raised about the safety issue of the abandoned property. Carte Blanche investigates.

Unique Selling Point:
On a fateful night of 21 October 2022 two young people from Stellenbosch lost their lives when their vehicle simply vanished in a water filled quarry on an abandoned property in Stellenbosch. 18-year-old Leila Du Preez Lees and 19-year-old Ethan Kirkland’s lifeless bodies were found three days later after an extensive search by the police and the community at large.

We investigate who was at fault. The owner, for not securing the property, or the municipality for not holding the owner accountable, or both.


Summary:
77 Bird street is a problem property and has been so for 30 years. The owners, Daniel de Canha, and his father Paul, bought the property from the St. Nicholas Catholic Church next door, and planned to build a block of flats. They applied for a multi-residential zone permit which was granted by the municipal council provided they met the requirements, one of them being to build a slip road to access the property. De Canha simply ignored the condition and started excavating to accommodate a 4-story basement parking on the property. Without building plan approval from the council construction was halted and the property left with a big gaping hole 10 meters deep by 30 meters wide. Over time the quarry filled with water and vegetation started growing.

According to Stuart Grobbelaar, spokesperson for Stellenboch municipality, several attempts were made to ‘engage with the property owner in order to expedite the development.’ Grobbelaar said they served them with a notice in March 2022 to get their required land use rights in order; drain and clean the property and erect a proper fence around the property. None of this was done.

Had the council followed the rules of the Problem Property By-Laws, approved by the Stellenbosch municipal council in July 2020, the owner should have been fined for non-compliance to maintain the property in a good state of repair and in a safe condition”. In addition De Canha was guilty of an offense in terms of the Stellenbosch Municipality By-Law (June 2023) as he did not comply with the Compliance Notice served on him within the period stated. This is tantamount to imprisonment and a hefty fine. Yet again, the municipality did not follow the rules.

Tragically two innocent people had to pay the price for gross misconduct and negligence of the owners and a slack attitude by the Stellenbosch Municipality.



Further information:
Leila’s mother, Annene du Preez, is heartbroken. She had appealed to the municipality to take steps against the owner and asked for the property to be made secure. “The fence can’t even keep a bicycle out”, she says.

Leila was to turn 19 three days after she died. She and Ethan Kirkland were a couple and they went out that night to celebrate. They were on their way home, a block away from 77 Bird street, when their Subaru SUV swerved off the road and disappeared into the water-filled quarry.

Ethan’s father, Paul Midlane, remembers his son as ‘the kindest person you have ever met’. He did not have a bad word for anybody. He loved playing his guitar and was excited about this new girlfriend, Leila. He has also appealed to the Municipality to “act with urgency and make that awful site safe and secure.”

Leila had one sister, Mila, who after a year, is still very traumatised about the loss of her younger sister. Ethan left behind two brothers who live in the UK with their mom.

“We have to face our daily lives without our children and thus our determination in this matter will only grow larger to ensure the safety for the many school children, other pedestrians and road users at that location, with the hope that something will be done before that site claims more lives,” says Annene.

After the incident, Annene had 8000 residents and students signing a petition demanding action from the council. In January 2023 the mayor responded to say several notices were served on the owner with no result and said the next step will be to go to court. In a council meeting held on the 25th of October, a year after the horrific incident, the municipality indicated that they will resort to instituting formal court proceedings to resolve the matter but raised their concern about the financial implications.

The owner, Daniel de Canha, is a businessman and owner of more than a dozen properties in Stellenbosch. Two more of the properties in Paradyskloof are also abandoned. The site is an eyesore with bricks lying around and totally neglected. This, says the estate agents, brings down the value of the neighbouring properties.

The story:
An interview with the Municipality to put them on the spot about the problem property and their lack of performance as the council against the owner who is clearly at fault here. We are hoping to get an interview with the owner, Daniel De Canha, although he has always declined interviews to the press in the past. We have his work address for a doorstep should it resort to that. We will interview Annene du Preez, Leila’s mother, and talk to Paul Middleton from Centurion, father of Ethan, on zoom. They will share their heartfelt memories of their children and disappointment in the lack of accountability by both the owner and the municipality. We will also hear from an estate agent, Hendrik Lemmer who has complaining to years to the municipality to do something about abandoned properties and in particular Bird street where the two young people lost their lives.
_________________________________________________________________________________________________


Extra Budget Items:
As agreed, R4500 will be donated to Annene du Preez, mother of Leila who died tragically last year. She lives in Knysna and will make a special trip to Stellenbosch for the interview. The funds will go towards her traveling cost and accommodation.

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT: Problem Properties
Duration: 10 minutes
Date: 28 November 2023

Bright music

1.V/O Stellenbosch - a student town surrounded by mountains and winelands.

pause…ominous music

2. V/O I’s a beautiful town where, more than a year ago, two young students died on this property in the bustling center.
pause
19-year-old Ethan Kirkland and Leila du Preez Lees, a year younger, went for a night out…and were never seen again.

UPS CCTV

3. V/O This CCTV footage shows some of their last moments: walking to their car and driving off. And then, later, another camera shows their car swerving and then, simply, disappearing.

Fade to black.

4. V/O For three days a baffled community searched for the missing couple. Nikita Roberts, a friend of Leila’s, joined the search.

Nikita Roberts: Leila’s friend - The Monday we organised people into groups and we started walking from Ethan’s house at the Niche which is 30 steps from the Groot Gat, the big hole and then 15 minutes after we started our search is when we found the debris.

5.V/O When the car was eventually found, Ethan’s father Paul Midlane, and Leila’s mother Annene Du Preez were called to the scene. It took several hours to get the car out of the pit.

Paul Midlane: Paul: Ethan’s father - you could hardly see that car. You could just see reeds and water… and then I knew.It’s hectic. I did not want to see it…The fact that they had to get divers to go in and fetch bodies in the middle of a suburb, in the middle of a city, is bizarre.

Annene du Preez: Leila’s mother - I did personally ask that if they were identified that they would allow me to hold her or at least see her…but in hindsight it wouldn’t have been a good idea because they had been under water for almost three days. But you just want to say “mom’s here, I found you”.

Erin Bates. Hold your child.

Annene du Preez: Yah..

Pause

6.V/O It's been a year since Leila and Ethan died. But who - if anyone - has been held to account?

7.V/O The quarry is on 77 Bird Street - a site belonging to the De Canha family: long-standing property owners from Stellenbosch.

Paulo and his son Daniel wanted to develop the site, but the municipality halted construction because a key condition hadn’t been met - the building of an access slip road.

LINK: 30 years ago the de Canha family planned to build a block of flats here on Bird street in central Stellenbosch. Without authorisation they went ahead to excavate for a four-story parking lot and all that remains is this hole.

8.V/O So, over three decades the 10 meter-deep, 30 meter-wide hole filled with rainwater and became overgrown with dense vegetation…surrounded only by a flimsy fence.

pause

9. V/O Among other things the town’s own municipal bylaws say a problem property is one that’s abandoned, derelict, and ‘dangerous to life or property’. If the Bird Street quarry doesn’t fit that definition, what does?
Pause
Going by the bylaw’s definition, we found that Bird Street isn’t the only problem property in the De Canhas’ portfolio. They have two more on the other side of town.

LINK: We are at another one of de Canha’s abandoned properties and you can see from all those bricks over there, clearly this development also didn’t get off the ground.

10. How could this be, a year after an unsecured hole in the ground claimed two young lives?
pause
In an email, Daniel told us his father, Paulo, was gravely ill, but he still intended to develop the property before he died. He said he’d submitted building plans but was waiting for rezoning from residential to mixed-use. He added that he’d soon be meeting the town planner as part of the regular feedback provided to municipal officials on good faith.

On why 77 Bird Street hadn’t been secured or why they’d ignored the municipal requirements to drain the water and close the hole we received no response.
pause
Daniel declined an on-camera interview, so we went in search of him.

LINK: The De Canha family own more than a dozen properties in Stellenbosch and several of them are on Bird Street behind me. We know that Daniel de Canha has an office in one of the buildings and we are going to see if maybe he is going to talk to us.

UPS: Erin Bates: Do you know where Daniel de Canha’s office is?

Erin Bates: Hi, I’m Erin from Carte Blanche, where is Daniel? We’re just trying to get some comments from 77 Bird Street. Can you give him a ring perhaps?

Daniel’s wife: Unfortunately I don’t have my phone with me.

UPS ….thank you

Erin Bates: So that was Daniel’s wife, Liezel, she says he is not available and will be in client meetings all day ... it is ringing. “You have reached the mailbox of Daniel de Canha”…
Daniel, this is Erin Bates from Carte Blanche……

11.V/O We left a message… and tried one final location: a business address listed for several De Canha companies.

Erin Bates: This is it no….. 21 hello….

12.V/O Clearly, Daniel wasn’t going to appear on camera.

So, if not him, who would provide the answers demanded by a community living with a death trap in their midst?

Under the law, municipalities have significant power to levy fines against the owners of properties where earthwork is unsafe or a danger to life. R100 a day for each day they’re in breach. Recently the Stellenbosch municipal council adopted its own Problem Property Bylaw which says that failing to keep a property in a good and safe condition should incur a fine, up to 3 years in jail, or both. In their response to us, the municipality didn’t mention exercising their right to levy penalties.

We asked for an interview with the municipality whose own by-laws had been - and continue to be - flouted. They declined but we decided to try again.

Erin Bates: Geraldine Mettler is the municipal manager for Stellenbosch. We are going to see if we can speak to her. She has an office inside this building.

UPS: Hello sussie, I am trying to get hold of Geraldine Mettler.

Erin Bates: No luck finding the municipal manager. Let’s see if we can get hold of the mayor.

13.V/O After a few minutes, Mayor Gesie van Deventer’s secretary emerged.

Secretary: She’s not here at the moment. I am not sure what I can do for you. I can only convey your message.

14.V/O Annene had experienced similar stone-walling: for months she’d sought answers about who bears responsibility for the infamous quarry.

Annene du Preez: I counted my phone calls at one point.. It was over 70 phone calls and during that I never got to speak to a single person on the other side.

15.V/O The day after our visit, the municipality messaged to say “The current Mayor and Administration have worked tirelessly to find an amicable solution to this matter. Unfortunately undertakings and promises made by the private owners have not been fully fulfilled and this necessitated Council to adopt a Council item to institute legal action”.

But it can take months - even years - for the law to take its course. And, in the interim, the municipality hasn’t said how it intends preventing further loss of life at the Bird Street site.

Annene du Preez: I am finding out what it would entail to lay criminal charges. Right now that hole doesn’t give anybody a second chance.

16. V/O Police have confirmed a case of culpable homicide is being investigated but provided no further detail.

Pause

17. V/O For the parents, grief continues to run deep….memories of their children as vivid as they were.

Erin Bates: Is there a particular moment, a holiday, a photo, a song that takes you back to celebrating her rather than what happened on that fateful night?

Annene du Preez: I would say just about everything does. You go into a bakery you see her favourite pastry and its tears and you go into a shop and see a beautiful set of earrings so the triggers are absolutely everywhere ...you know the change of seasons.

Paul Midlane: He’s gone. Nothing is going to bring him back. I am still trying to process that he is dead and expect him to call me tomorrow so I never want another parent to go through what I am going through.
____________________________________________________________________________

PROMO 1: (21 SECONDS)
V/O They call it the Big Hole, an abandoned property in central Stellenbosch which led to the death of two young people.

UPS: Paul Midlane: He’s gone. Nothing is going to bring him back

V/O Yet no-one has been held accountable.

PROMO 2: (21 SECONDS)
V/O Two young people paid the ultimate price when their SUV plunged into a deep pit filled with water on an abandoned property in central Stellenbosch.

UPS: Paul Midlane: its a swamp, a pit, a quarry… just take some responsibility to make it safer.

PROMO 3: (21 SECONDS)
V/O When the bodies of two teenagers were pulled out of a water filled quarry in an abandoned property in central Stellenbosch, grieving parents searched for answers.

Annene Du Preez: It is just such a death trap just waiting. And I just can’t let it go until I know the perimeter is secure.

PROMO 4: (21 SECONDS)
VO: An abandoned property in the heart of Stellenbosch.

Paul Midlane - I can’t believe, what is it doing there. It is this pit of a quarry..

VO: A death trap linked to the killing of two young people.

Annene du Preez: This hole is older than our children’s lives.

VO: So, who’s responsible for their untimely deaths?

Without authorisation they went ahead to excavate for a four-story parking lot and all that remains is this hole. 8.V/O So, over three decades the 10 meter-deep, 30 meter-wide hole filled with rainwater and became overgrown with dense vegetation…surrounded only by a flimsy fence. pause 9. V/O Among other things the town’s own municipal bylaws say a problem property is one that’s abandoned, derelict, and ‘dangerous to life or property’. If the Bird Street quarry doesn’t fit that definition, what does? Pause Going by the bylaw’s definition, we found that Bird Street isn’t the only problem property in the De Canhas’ portfolio. They have two more on the other side of town. LINK: We are at another one of de Canha’s abandoned properties and you can see from all those bricks over there, clearly this development also didn’t get off the ground. 10. How could this be, a year after an unsecured hole in the ground claimed two young lives? pause In an email, Daniel told us his father, Paulo, was gravely ill, but he still intended to develop the property before he died. He said he’d submitted building plans but was waiting for rezoning from residential to mixed-use. He added that he’d soon be meeting the town planner as part of the regular feedback provided to municipal officials on good faith. On why 77 Bird Street hadn’t been secured or why they’d ignored the municipal requirements to drain the water and close the hole we received no response. pause Daniel declined an on-camera interview, so we went in search of him. LINK: The De Canha family own more than a dozen properties in Stellenbosch and several of them are on Bird Street behind me. We know that Daniel de Canha has an office in one of the buildings and we are going to see if maybe he is going to talk to us. UPS: Erin Bates: Do you know where Daniel de Canha’s office is? Erin Bates: Hi, I’m Erin from Carte Blanche, where is Daniel? We’re just trying to get some comments from 77 Bird Street. Can you give him a ring perhaps? Daniel’s wife: Unfortunately I don’t have my phone with me. UPS ….thank you Erin Bates: So that was Daniel’s wife, Liezel, she says he is not available and will be in client meetings all day ... it is ringing. “You have reached the mailbox of Daniel de Canha”… Daniel, this is Erin Bates from Carte Blanche…… 11.V/O We left a message… and tried one final location: a business address listed for several De Canha companies. Erin Bates: This is it no….. 21 hello…. 12.V/O Clearly, Daniel wasn’t going to appear on camera. So, if not him, who would provide the answers demanded by a community living with a death trap in their midst? Under the law, municipalities have significant power to levy fines against the owners of properties where earthwork is unsafe or a danger to life. R100 a day for each day they’re in breach. Recently the Stellenbosch municipal council adopted its own Problem Property Bylaw which says that failing to keep a property in a good and safe condition should incur a fine, up to 3 years in jail, or both. In their response to us, the municipality didn’t mention exercising their right to levy penalties. We asked for an interview with the municipality whose own by-laws had been - and continue to be - flouted. They declined but we decided to try again. Erin Bates: Geraldine Mettler is the municipal manager for Stellenbosch. We are going to see if we can speak to her. She has an office inside this building. UPS: Hello sussie, I am trying to get hold of Geraldine Mettler. Erin Bates: No luck finding the municipal manager. Let’s see if we can get hold of the mayor. 13.V/O After a few minutes, Mayor Gesie van Deventer’s secretary emerged. Secretary: She’s not here at the moment. I am not sure what I can do for you. I can only convey your message. 14.V/O Annene had experienced similar stone-walling: for months she’d sought answers about who bears responsibility for the infamous quarry. Annene du Preez: I counted my phone calls at one point.. It was over 70 phone calls and during that I never got to speak to a single person on the other side. 15.V/O The day after our visit, the municipality messaged to say “The current Mayor and Administration have worked tirelessly to find an amicable solution to this matter. Unfortunately undertakings and promises made by the private owners have not been fully fulfilled and this necessitated Council to adopt a Council item to institute legal action”. But it can take months - even years - for the law to take its course. And, in the interim, the municipality hasn’t said how it intends preventing further loss of life at the Bird Street site. Annene du Preez: I am finding out what it would entail to lay criminal charges. Right now that hole doesn’t give anybody a second chance. 16. V/O Police have confirmed a case of culpable homicide is being investigated but provided no further detail. Pause 17. V/O For the parents, grief continues to run deep….memories of their children as vivid as they were. Erin Bates: Is there a particular moment, a holiday, a photo, a song that takes you back to celebrating her rather than what happened on that fateful night? Annene du Preez: I would say just about everything does. You go into a bakery you see her favourite pastry and its tears and you go into a shop and see a beautiful set of earrings so the triggers are absolutely everywhere ...you know the change of seasons. Paul Midlane: He’s gone. Nothing is going to bring him back. I am still trying to process that he is dead and expect him to call me tomorrow so I never want another parent to go through what I am going through. ____________________________________________________________________________ PROMO 1: (21 SECONDS) V/O They call it the Big Hole, an abandoned property in central Stellenbosch which led to the death of two young people. UPS: Paul Midlane: He’s gone. Nothing is going to bring him back V/O Yet no-one has been held accountable. PROMO 2: (21 SECONDS) V/O Two young people paid the ultimate price when their SUV plunged into a deep pit filled with water on an abandoned property in central Stellenbosch. UPS: Paul Midlane: its a swamp, a pit, a quarry… just take some responsibility to make it safer. PROMO 3: (21 SECONDS) V/O When the bodies of two teenagers were pulled out of a water filled quarry in an abandoned property in central Stellenbosch, grieving parents searched for answers. Annene Du Preez: It is just such a death trap just waiting. And I just can’t let it go until I know the perimeter is secure. PROMO 4: (21 SECONDS) VO: An abandoned property in the heart of Stellenbosch. Paul Midlane - I can’t believe, what is it doing there. It is this pit of a quarry.. VO: A death trap linked to the killing of two young people. Annene du Preez: This hole is older than our children’s lives. VO: So, who’s responsible for their untimely deaths? ________________________________________________________________________________________________

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): When a deathtrap excavation site claimed the lives of two young people, questions were raised about the safety issue of the abandoned property. Carte Blanche investigates.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: On a fateful night of 21 October 2022 two young people from Stellenbosch lost their lives when their vehicle simply vanished in a water filled quarry on an abandoned property in Stellenbosch. 18-year-old Leila Du Preez Lees and 19-year-old Ethan Kirkland’s lifeless bodies were found three days later after an extensive search by the police and the community at large. We investigate who was at fault. The owner, for not securing the property, or the municipality for not holding the owner accountable, or both.
metadata.Summary: 77 Bird street is a problem property and has been so for 30 years. The owners, Daniel de Canha, and his father Paul, bought the property from the St. Nicholas Catholic Church next door, and planned to build a block of flats. They applied for a multi-residential zone permit which was granted by the municipal council provided they met the requirements, one of them being to build a slip road to access the property. De Canha simply ignored the condition and started excavating to accommodate a 4-story basement parking on the property. Without building plan approval from the council construction was halted and the property left with a big gaping hole 10 meters deep by 30 meters wide. Over time the quarry filled with water and vegetation started growing. According to Stuart Grobbelaar, spokesperson for Stellenboch municipality, several attempts were made to ‘engage with the property owner in order to expedite the development.’ Grobbelaar said they served them with a notice in March 2022 to get their required land use rights in order; drain and clean the property and erect a proper fence around the property. None of this was done. Had the council followed the rules of the Problem Property By-Laws, approved by the Stellenbosch municipal council in July 2020, the owner should have been fined for non-compliance to maintain the property in a good state of repair and in a safe condition”. In addition De Canha was guilty of an offense in terms of the Stellenbosch Municipality By-Law (June 2023) as he did not comply with the Compliance Notice served on him within the period stated. This is tantamount to imprisonment and a hefty fine. Yet again, the municipality did not follow the rules. Tragically two innocent people had to pay the price for gross misconduct and negligence of the owners and a slack attitude by the Stellenbosch Municipality.
metadata.Further information: Leila’s mother, Annene du Preez, is heartbroken. She had appealed to the municipality to take steps against the owner and asked for the property to be made secure. “The fence can’t even keep a bicycle out”, she says. Leila was to turn 19 three days after she died. She and Ethan Kirkland were a couple and they went out that night to celebrate. They were on their way home, a block away from 77 Bird street, when their Subaru SUV swerved off the road and disappeared into the water-filled quarry. Ethan’s father, Paul Midlane, remembers his son as ‘the kindest person you have ever met’. He did not have a bad word for anybody. He loved playing his guitar and was excited about this new girlfriend, Leila. He has also appealed to the Municipality to “act with urgency and make that awful site safe and secure.” Leila had one sister, Mila, who after a year, is still very traumatised about the loss of her younger sister. Ethan left behind two brothers who live in the UK with their mom. “We have to face our daily lives without our children and thus our determination in this matter will only grow larger to ensure the safety for the many school children, other pedestrians and road users at that location, with the hope that something will be done before that site claims more lives,” says Annene. After the incident, Annene had 8000 residents and students signing a petition demanding action from the council. In January 2023 the mayor responded to say several notices were served on the owner with no result and said the next step will be to go to court. In a council meeting held on the 25th of October, a year after the horrific incident, the municipality indicated that they will resort to instituting formal court proceedings to resolve the matter but raised their concern about the financial implications. The owner, Daniel de Canha, is a businessman and owner of more than a dozen properties in Stellenbosch. Two more of the properties in Paradyskloof are also abandoned. The site is an eyesore with bricks lying around and totally neglected. This, says the estate agents, brings down the value of the neighbouring properties. The story: An interview with the Municipality to put them on the spot about the problem property and their lack of performance as the council against the owner who is clearly at fault here. We are hoping to get an interview with the owner, Daniel De Canha, although he has always declined interviews to the press in the past. We have his work address for a doorstep should it resort to that. We will interview Annene du Preez, Leila’s mother, and talk to Paul Middleton from Centurion, father of Ethan, on zoom. They will share their heartfelt memories of their children and disappointment in the lack of accountability by both the owner and the municipality. We will also hear from an estate agent, Hendrik Lemmer who has complaining to years to the municipality to do something about abandoned properties and in particular Bird street where the two young people lost their lives. _________________________________________________________________________________________________
metadata.Extra Budget Items: As agreed, R4500 will be donated to Annene du Preez, mother of Leila who died tragically last year. She lives in Knysna and will make a special trip to Stellenbosch for the interview. The funds will go towards her traveling cost and accommodation.
metadata.Other Footage Sources: CCTV camera footage of the block of flats where Ethan Kirkland lived; SUV leaving the parking lot; SUV coming around the street corner and disappearing in the hole on 77 Bird street.
metadata.Reason for legal: We are putting the owner of the problem property on the spot for not securing his property which lead to the death of two young people. We are also questioning the Stellenbosch municipality about their lack of action against the owner of a problem that started 30 years ago.
